lab.name: Intelligent Energy Systems & Sustainable Technologies Lab
lab.parent: International Council for Research & Innovation in Science, Technology & Engineering (ICRI-STE)
lab.theme: AI, Renewable Energy, Smart Grids, Energy Storage, Digital Twins & Intelligent Control
lab.proposition: Develop AI-enabled intelligent energy systems that can predict renewable generation and energy demand, optimise storage and power flows, and autonomously manage renewable-powered microgrids for a more efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy future.

project: AI-Enabled Intelligent Renewable Energy and Smart Microgrid Systems for Sustainable Energy Management
layers: Solar PV, wind energy and hybrid renewable generation.
Battery energy storage, battery-management system and charging/discharging controller.
Voltage, current, power, generation, battery status, temperature, demand and environmental conditions.
Real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, rapid prediction, low-latency control and reduced communication needs.
Renewable and demand forecasting, battery prediction, anomaly detection, optimisation and intelligent control.
A continuously updated computational representation of the physical energy system.
Optimal generation utilisation, battery charging/discharging, grid interaction, demand response and energy allocation.
objectives: AI/ML models for solar PV generation, wind generation, renewable-energy availability and short-term energy production.
Predictive models using historical consumption, weather, time, seasonal patterns and occupancy/usage information where available.
AI-driven state-of-charge and state-of-health estimation, charging/discharging optimisation, degradation-aware scheduling and storage utilisation.
Algorithms coordinating solar, wind, battery, grid and loads under operational constraints and energy costs.
Reinforcement learning and other adaptive control approaches for real-time energy management.
A computational twin for monitoring, simulation, prediction, optimisation, scenario analysis and decision support.
A prototype energy-management platform evaluated under realistic operating scenarios.
applications: AI-based generation forecasting, predictive maintenance and optimisation.
Energy-demand prediction and intelligent energy management.
AI-controlled energy consumption and demand response.
Solar-powered irrigation and intelligent energy management.
AI-based charging optimisation and battery-grid coordination.
Distributed renewable energy, storage and demand management.
risks: Solar and wind generation are uncertain.
Excessive cycling can reduce battery life.
Incorrect predictions could lead to poor control decisions.
Hybrid AI + physics-based modelling, uncertainty estimation and safety constraints.
Complex AI models may be difficult to deploy at the edge.
Model compression, lightweight architectures and edge optimisation.
Real energy systems have safety and operational constraints.
Progressive validation: simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, controlled prototype, field demonstration.
phases: Target application, system configuration, constraints, data and performance requirements, industrial KPIs.
Models for renewable generation, demand, batteries, microgrid operation and energy flows.
Forecasting, anomaly-detection, battery-intelligence, optimisation and control algorithms.
The computational representation of the energy system.
Sensors, IoT, edge computing, AI, energy management and visualisation.
problems: Increasing integration of intermittent renewable energy
Uncertainty in solar and wind generation
Energy losses and inefficient power management
Increasing complexity of distributed energy resources
Increasing requirements for sustainable and low-carbon energy systems
